scenario: LSER.16.9: a `sliding` `rate` over one sample reads `null` -- no elapsed time to divide by -- and over two reads (last - first) / elapsed_seconds. Drives the companion read `s.rate` of a `sliding` declaration, which the compiler puts on the raw-sample backing (SeriesBackendRingBuffer): libds's `ds_series_ring_buffer_rate`, Mercury's `aggregate(agg_rate)`. A `ttl` schema (LSER.7.6.3). 10 at 0 s, 30 at 1 s, then a third assert; reads pre-sample (LSER.8.6.1): cold, [10] null (no log), [10, 30] 20.0. THE `where` READS A SERIES, SO IT IS RE-READ EVERY PUMP ([LTIM.2.4.1]) and each live fact fires once, on the pump its condition first holds ([LTIM.2.5.1]): at the third pump the two facts before read 20.0 with it, so `r 20.0` logs three times.
rules_ds:
use default

schema Sample scope ttl 1_d:
    dev: String
    level: Int

series Sample.level (by: dev):
    rate sliding 1_h

rule r:
    Sample s where s.rate is not null
->
    log info "r {s.rate}"
